config.title: Debounced Search

intro.title: Debounced Search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that filters a list of items as the user types, using a technique called debouncing. Debouncing delays the search execution until the user pauses typing, preventing excessive API calls or re-renders for every keystroke. You'll learn to implement this using React hooks like useState for state management and useEffect for side effects, along with a setTimeout function. By the end, you'll understand how to create a responsive and efficient search feature in a React TypeScript application.
intro.usecase: Debounced search is essential in modern web applications where real-time filtering improves user experience without overwhelming servers. You'll find this pattern in e-commerce sites like Amazon or eBay, where search suggestions appear as you type without sending excessive API calls. Dashboard interfaces with live data filtering, admin panels with user search, and form autocomplete fields all rely on debouncing to balance responsiveness with performance. As a developer, implementing debounced search prevents unnecessary network requests and provides smoother interactions for end users.

objectives: Initialize a React component with TypeScript interfaces for search state
Implement a controlled input component for search queries
Configure a debounced function using setTimeout and clearTimeout
Bind the debounced function to input change events
Update component state with the latest search value after debouncing
Render search results based on the debounced query
Integrate cleanup logic to prevent memory leaks from pending timers

successCriteria: searchQuery state is declared using useState with an empty string initial value.

steps.title: Create a timeout reference with useRef
steps.instruction: Inside the SearchComponent, create a timeout reference using useRef to store the setTimeout ID. Initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Call useRef with an initial value of null and store it in a variable named timeoutRef.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a timeoutRef variable initialized with useRef to hold the timer ID.
successCriteria: A timeoutRef variable is declared using useRef and initialized with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useRef with an initial value of null and storing it in a variable named timeoutRef.

steps.title: Define the handleSearchChange event handler
steps.instruction: Inside the SearchComponent, create a function named handleSearchChange that takes an event parameter and updates searchQuery with the input value.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> and calls setSearchQuery with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSearchChange function is defined that updates the searchQuery state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The handleSearchChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setSearchQuery with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it takes an event parameter and calls setSearchQuery with the input value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSearchChange function is not defined correctly. It should update searchQuery with the input value from the event.

steps.title: Set up the debouncing logic with useEffect
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook that sets a timeout to update debouncedQuery after searchQuery changes, and clears the previous timeout on cleanup.
steps.hint: Use the useEffect hook with searchQuery as a dependency. Inside, set a timeout with setTimeout that calls setDebouncedQuery after a delay (e.g., 500ms). Store the timeout ID in timeoutRef.current and clear it in the cleanup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is implemented with proper timeout management to debounce searchQuery updates.
successCriteria: A useEffect hook is added with searchQuery as a dependency, sets a timeout to update debouncedQuery, and clears the timeout on cleanup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect includes both the timeout setup and cleanup. Check that you're using timeoutRef.current to store and clear the timeout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debouncing logic isn't fully implemented. Remember to use useEffect with searchQuery as a dependency, set a timeout that calls setDebouncedQuery, and clear the previous timeout in the cleanup function.
